Observed at +17.642026901245117s — page 7
eanings: a short `429` is the per-minute\n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Ret
ry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means\n> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting

will never help.

**User testing** (`/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,
`.../studies/...`) — publishin
g an environment for real visitors, reading what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironm

ent: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environmen
ts/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Proje
ct **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted:
false` when there was nothing published |\n| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../s
tudies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studi
es/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{s
tudyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studi
es/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{study
Id}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{member
IdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point

the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who alr
eady used it.** It stops the\n> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the
single most important thing to know here, because rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not

undo the
> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live se
ssions rather than waiting for\n> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump\n> the study's `acces
sVersion`, and a session minted under an older version\n> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invit

ed
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update an

d
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass
over the

m. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpo
int | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real
\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the se
ssions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in t
he current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this st
udy, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means n
obody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insig
htsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/ins
ights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/
dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |\n| `POST .../studies/{study

Id}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,
`p
ending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` expla
in incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `proj

ectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe
the map independently. Reading this response never starts analysis.

Taxonomy en
tries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older a
ssignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached

reassignment completes. These are
current views with version provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncat
ed` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a\nwhole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, sco
pe totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection cont

ributes to the unmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open obje
cts** on purpose.\nTheir upstream projections grow with the product and the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list

would turn every new metric into a spec
violation. Read what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting ins
ights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.\n> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and
swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deli

berately takes a second slice, which is
> why it is never inferred from anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MC

PJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capabil
ity note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }
`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`4
29` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictly — an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored;
the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goes to the MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180

days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.
> Include the failing cal
l's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it lets the team find that request in the server logs. An identical repor

t
> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**

Planning** — one read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../projects/{proj

ectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, the beta gate's state, plan limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `
capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write still enforces\n> independently, so a `true` here that races a flag f
lip costs you a clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect success — and nothing should consult it\n> *instead of* trying. It exists
because agent surfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is built with no organization in hand, so the alternative is\n> attempti

ng the write and reading the failure, by which point the agent has
> usually already told someone what it was about to do.

The
same surface is available as an [OpenAPI\nspecification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspector/main/docs/reference/o

penapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **a
ccounts**. When your test users\ncan't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every d

ay, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token
to a named account before each run.
